articles.title: Gore, gimps and a potty-mouthed magpie: welcome to the Lisbon horror festival where nightmares are a dream
articles.summary: MotelX – Portugal’s only film festival dedicated to horror – hopes to inspire local film-makers by showcasing world-class scares. Now in its 20th edition, its directors say truly nerve-shredding cinema is its holy grail.
body: I f horror happens in the dark, the midnight movie showing was once the perfect way of gauging the genre’s health. But those days may be over. “When we were a film club, our first ever cinema screening was Takashi Miike’s Ichi the Killer in 2003, and it was full,” says Pedro Souto, co-director of Lisbon’s horror-centric MotelX festival. “But you don’t have that many people at midnight any more. I don’t know why.” He’s right: the midnight slot I attend – of the gore-bathed Indonesian kung fu flick Ikatan Darah – is only half full. Only a few appreciative chuckles when meat-cleavers plunge into craniums suggest the old midnight spirit still lives.
points: MotelX – Portugal’s only film festival dedicated to horror – hopes to inspire local film-makers by showcasing world-class scares.
Now in its 20th edition, its directors say truly nerve-shredding cinema is its holy grail.

articles.title: ‘Like ‘Amores Perros,’ I Hope My Film Will Also Transcend Time in Some Way,’ Says Gael García Bernal of His Third Directorial Outing, ‘Hombre al Agua’
articles.summary: Gael García Bernal is best known for his breakout roles in two of Mexico’s most consequential films, “Amores Perros” (2000) and “Y Tu Mama Tambien” (2001) but he’s also been directing these past years.
body: In “Hombre al agua,” García Bernal plays Camilo, a Cuban lifeguard who saves Abel, a Mexican businessman, from drowning. Grateful, Abel brings him to Mexico to work as his right-hand man and introduces him to his daughter, Juana, whom Camilo later marries. But he gradually realizes that his new life is part of a carefully orchestrated plan. As questions emerge about Abel’s motives, Camilo begins to piece together what is really happening and decides to take control of his future.
As the title suggests, roughly translated to “man overboard,” Camilo is adrift as his marriage falls apart and he tries to move beyond the lie he’s been living.

“I also wanted to explore the crisis of masculinity, the roles of men and women within a couple, and the experience of separation. I wanted to do all of this through comedy, with a kind of meta-cinematic playfulness, while also looking at the political landscape in Latin America today: where we are, what is happening and where we are going,” he said.
Reflecting on the impact of “Amores Perros,” he mused: “When it came out, it became something extraordinary and transcended time. Twenty-five years later, we’re still celebrating it.”

articles.title: Stephanie Ahn’s Seven-Year Road to ‘Bedford Park’: ‘You Never Know What Can Make Your Film Better’
articles.summary: After winning the U.S. Dramatic Special Jury Award for Debut Feature at Sundance this year, “Bedford Park” has its international premiere at the Toronto Film Festival, ahead of a U.S. theatrical release by Sony Pictures Classics.
body: This tension is embodied by Audrey, a physical therapist with a repressed fighting spirit and slightly kinky sexual encounters. When she meets Eli, a Korean American adoptee, in not-so-ideal circumstances, their relationship blossoms into a romance that redefines them. The story unfolds in the New Jersey suburbs, where Audrey goes back to live with her parents.

“I auditioned for Audrey seven years ago,” remembers Moon Choi. “It’s rare but Stephanie arranged to send me the whole script ahead of the audition. I read it in one sitting.” This project has been the longest the actress has ever waited to film, as COVID, Hollywood strikes and lack of funding kept threatening production. “I grew old with Audrey,” adds Choi. “I was 31 when I was cast and filmed at 37. It changed my understanding of many scenes.”

Throughout, the script remained the project’s fixed point. It changed considerably over the years, shifting from a family drama into a love story. “I didn’t want a traditional love story. I wanted to make the feeling of them getting together feel inevitable — but not predictable,” says Ahn.

articles.title: Jimmy Kimmel in Talks to Renew Late-Night Show at ABC
articles.summary: Jimmy Kimmel and Disney’s ABC have entered into negotiations about keeping the host in late-night after the new TV season, a process that might ordinarily be the most normal of business practices, but in the current climate is exceedingly fraught.
body: A single-year contract would give both host and broadcaster more flexibility to change plans if the business of wee-hours TV grew more challenged.
Puck previously reported that Kimmel and the Disney TV network had entered into renewal talks.

The talks are likely to touch upon some difficult realities. Spending on late night television shows hit $209 million in 2025, according to data from Guideline, a tracker of ad expenditures, down from $519.7 million in 2017. Ad spending on “Jimmy Kimmel Live” totaled $51.1 million in 2024, accounting for 21% of all late night spend, according to the firm — a percentage that is well behind that for NBC’s “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon” and CBS’ now defunct “The Late Show with Stephen Colbert.”

articles.summary: The “Point Break” followup series has officially been ordered at AMC and AMC+, Variety has learned. The modern update of the beloved 1991 action film was first reported to be in the works at the network back in December 2025.
body: The logline for the series states, “More than three decades after the events of the original ‘Point Break’ film, a new heist crew inspired by the Ex-Presidents has emerged and the FBI must rely on a mysterious ex-pro surfer with a checkered past to infiltrate them.”

Dave Kalstein and Christopher C. Rogers serve as co-showrunners and executive producers on the series. Alcon co-founders and co-CEOs Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson executive produce, as do Alcon Television Group head Ben Roberts and Julia Cohen. M-K Kennedy, Paul Gilbert and Daniel Gratton are overseeing the project for StudioCanal. Steven Johnson, Diego Piasek, and Gene Hong will serve as co-executive producers, with Emily Yoshida and Ben Cook as supervising producers.

articles.title: ‘They know the house they are bombing is full of children’: NAZA’s directors on their devastating film about Israeli intelligence
articles.summary: Rachel Szor and Yuval Abraham collected the testimony of 24 insiders who helped remotely target Gazans’ homes. They explain how they got these self-professed ‘small cogs’ to talk about the killing. On a darkened rooftop in Tel Aviv, Israeli intelligence officers outline the details of their work.
body: I meet Szor and Abraham at the Venice film festival, where NAZA is competing for the Golden Lion award. The pair won an Oscar for their previous documentary, 2024’s No Other Land (co-directed with Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal), which spotlighted Palestinian resistance in the occupied West Bank. “No Other Land documented horrible crimes,” Abraham says. “But at the same time it gave people … I don’t want to say hope, but some light to latch on to. It’s not a coincidence that this film is all in the dark. We are in a very dark place right now.”

articles.title: ‘Danny Boyle, please make another film about drugs’: Venice film festival’s feedback wall takes no prisoners
articles.summary: The written forum allows members of the public to vent their fury at the movies they’ve seen – and the festival organisers. In an industry that is reliant on the fickle vagaries of taste, film festivals exist to establish facts.
body: Film festivals, in turn, need beautiful A-listers to attract coverage and sponsorship, and hence there is a constant risk that these annual events become gigantic hype machines, in which every turkey is a classic and every half-hearted performance a masterclass.

Which is why there may not be a more important institution in world cinema than the Venice film festival’s Ridateci i soldi (“Give us our money back”): a makeshift chipboard wall erected next to the Palazzo del Cinema on which visitors are encouraged – with the blessing of the management – to scribble complaints and hatchet jobs in the most scathing terms possible.

The wall’s 30-year tradition commands that the festival’s director Alberto Barbera has to personally hand out a prize to the meanest diatribe, making Venice’s wall of shame a barrier against hype, an institutionalised pricking of the film world’s own pomposity.

On the Lido this year, there were complaints about the rising cost of entry badges, water taxis and local accommodation (“Maybe by 2030 we’ll have to pay for the oxygen we breathe”), queue lengths, uncomfortable seats and ceiling lights going on in the screening rooms.

articles.title: Farmer left in abandoned, freezing town without food and water for TV show
articles.summary: Ioan Humphreys said he had "zero idea" about what he was getting into in the survival show.
body: A farmer from mid Wales was dropped into an abandoned American town with no food, water, electricity or tools for a new series.
Apocalypse, which starts on Sunday, sees two groups of strangers attempt to survive in a site usually used to train military, with whatever they can find while competing for limited resources.
Ioan Humphreys, from Carno, told BBC Wales he had "zero idea" what he was getting into and was only told it was a survival show about a month before filming.
The 33-year-old was dropped into the town with nothing but the clothes he was wearing - with temperatures dropping as low as -12C (10F) during the challenge.

articles.title: Bids encouraged to keep famed artwork in the UK
articles.summary: Sir Stanley Spencer is synonymous with Cookham, where he was born, lived and set some of his work.
body: A painting by one of Britain's leading 20th Century artists must stay in the country in the hope that one of its galleries or institutions will buy it, the government said.
Sir Stanley Spencer, who was born and spent most of his life in Cookham, Berkshire, is probably best known for the series of artworks he created on the theme of resurrection.

The Resurrection of the Good and the Bad, finished in 1915, is the first piece exploring that topic and is an "immensely valuable" piece to use in the study of his work, the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) said.
Bids for the painting, with a recommended price of £450,000, will be welcomed until mid-December.

articles.title: Being Heumann review – Coda director’s disability rights drama is well-intentioned but clunky
articles.summary: Toronto film festival: the rousing story of Judith Heumann makes for obvious dramatic fodder and at times this biopic finds a rebellious groove but too much feels cut-and-paste.
body: O n my way to Toronto, I wheeled my suitcase toward the taxi that would take me to the airport, finding the curb cut in the sidewalk so that my luggage could roll seamlessly down to the street. What a nice convenience provided by municipal governments all over the United States, one that so many of us take wholly for granted.

Being Heumann is Heder’s follow-up to the Oscar-winning Coda, a film about a mixed family of deaf and hearing people significant in film history for centering disability so prominently and being handsomely rewarded for it. That is a woefully rare occurrence in Hollywood, though Coda (and its contemporary, Sound of Metal ) has had a noticeable impact on deaf representation on screen in the years since. Heder would thus seem the ideal steward for another film highlighting the lives and passions of physically marginalized people, who for so terribly long were essentially cut off from the rest of society because they lacked safe, proper access to public spaces.

articles.title: Stacey Solomon and Alesha Dixon to host The Voice UK in ITV revamp
articles.summary: The pair replace Emma Willis, who has hosted the show since 2014 but is leaving to front Strictly.
body: Alesha Dixon and Stacey Solomon are to host The Voice UK as part of a revamp of the show announced by ITV.
The pair replace Emma Willis, who has presented the singing contest since 2014 but recently left to front the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing.
ITV also confirmed earlier reports that singer Cheryl and rapper Aitch will join the The Voice as coaches, sitting in the show's famous giant red chairs.
It comes after Sir Tom Jones said earlier this week that he had been removed from the series despite wanting to stay, over an insurance issue.
